summary: The narrator leaves work feeling unwell and is confronted by coworker David in the elevator and lobby, who insists she use her health insurance. She stops at the Duane Reade pharmacy, where the pharmacist Bernd asks perceptive questions about her symptoms, including earlier fertility drugs and toad venom linked to Alex Goddard, and gives her a small boxed product. At home she reads the instructions, takes a hot bath, and then reaches for the phone.
one_line: A narrator feeling unwell gets pharmacy advice from Bernd after a coworker urges her to see a doctor, then takes a bath and reaches for the phone.
key_facts: The narrator ran into David on the elevator while coming down from the floor above after locking up.
David asked 'How's it going?' while ostentatiously checking his watch, with an approving gleam in his eyes.
David told the narrator, 'I pay for your health insurance. Use it, for God's sake.'
The narrator decided to stop at the Duane Reade on her corner and talk to the pharmacist after realizing this was no typical down day.
The pharmacist on second shift was a gray-haired portly old guy whose jacket tag said 'Bernd'.
The narrator sometimes called Bernd 'Dr. Bernd' by way of banter, but nothing she did could make him smile.
The narrator poured out her symptoms to Bernd, including a story about being given fertility drugs and toad venom.
The narrator wondered whether the past was coming back to haunt her in the form of the 'dark hand of Alex Goddard'.
Bernd walked around the counter and handed her a small, shrink-wrapped box, telling her to try it and come back tomorrow.
At home, the narrator collapsed onto the couch, opened the box, and read the instructions before following them.
The narrator filled the tub, added bubble-bath, placed the cordless phone on the toilet seat, and got into the bath.
The narrator ends the passage by reaching for the phone after the bath.

entities.name: David
entities.role: coworker who notices the narrator looks unwell, comments on her long hours, and tells her to use her health insurance

entities.name: Bernd
entities.role: gray-haired portly second-shift pharmacist at the Duane Reade who gives the narrator a boxed product and advice

entities.name: Alex Goddard
entities.role: figure the narrator associates with the 'dark hand' that may be causing her problems, linked to her fertility drugs and toad venom story

entities.name: Duane Reade
entities.role: pharmacy on the narrator's corner where she consults the pharmacist
